newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Profit-taking pulls India GDRs back.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Profit-taking pulls India GDRs back.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts succumbed to profit-taking on Tuesday, after a recent strong run ahead of the weekend's resolution to a three week political crisis and following a flat Bombay performance.
Traders and brokers said GDR premiums to the local market had risen sharply over recent days, leaving little room for further upside without a strong run in local market stocks.
They said the GDR market should consolidate in line with Bombay in coming days, with the focus moving from politics to corporate earnings and economics.
"Premiums on pivotals have expanded and buyers are hesitating to chase prices higher on quality GDRs already on high premiums," said a broker.
Stocks in Bombay fell earlier on profit-taking, with new Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral expected to win a confidence vote later on Tuesday.
The focus in the local market was on Reliance, which reported above-consensus annual results, but traders said the share had registered most of its gains on Monday.
Reliance shed 67 cents to $18.75/$19.75, SBI made 30 cents to $23.50/$24.50 and Hindalco fell 87 cents to $32.25/$33.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.74 points, or 2.14 percent, down at 79.54, with the premium over the local market at 19.73 percent from 23.35 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 0.84 points to 3,800.63.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.37 points to 126.46, representing a discount to the local market of 3.57 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.32 points, or 2.05 percent, down at 63.34, a premium of 32.25 percent over the local market.
